title: Power toys and Apples Boot Camp F15 and F16 remapping with side effects...

status.label: Boot Camp driver side effects are outside the current hook's control
status.detail: A maintainer explains that the low-level keyboard hook cannot suppress Boot Camp's lower-level F15/F16 processing while passing the remapped keys through; the reporter confirmed the issue persists.

judgment.rationale: The reporter confirms that Boot Camp continues to generate Print Screen, Scroll Lock, and Pause from the physical F14-F16 keys after Keyboard Manager remaps them. A maintainer explains that the low-level keyboard hook forwards keys to lower-level drivers and may not be able to suppress Boot Camp's additional actions while still delivering the remapped output; doing so would require a keyboard driver, which is not an available implementation path. The reporter confirmed in October 2024 that the behavior persists, but no PowerToys-side fix is supported by the current architecture.
evidence: The report lists PowerToys 0.57.2 and Apple Boot Camp drivers 6.0.6136; remapped F15/F16 still trigger Scroll Lock/Pause.
The reporter clarified that F14-F19 are available on a full-size Apple keyboard and confirmed the side effects occur only on a Mac running Windows through Boot Camp.
A maintainer explains that Keyboard Manager uses a low-level keyboard hook and cannot reliably block lower-level driver processing while passing intended keystrokes onward.
The reporter confirmed the issue still occurred in October 2024; no feasible filter-driver implementation or linked fix was found.
judgment.recommended_action: Do not propose a competing Keyboard Manager fix without a supported driver-level interception design; retain the documented Boot Camp limitation and revisit only if a feasible platform mechanism becomes available.

fix_assessment.rationale: The unwanted keys are generated by the Boot Camp driver below the current low-level keyboard hook. Suppressing that driver output while preserving remapped input would require a keyboard filter driver, which maintainers have said is not currently an available option.

issue_context.summary: On Windows running under Apple Boot Camp, F14-F16 remaps reportedly still trigger the Boot Camp driver’s Print Screen, Scroll Lock, and Pause actions.
known_information: The report lists PowerToys 0.57.2 and Apple Boot Camp drivers 6.0.6136.
The reporter clarified the Apple keyboard F14-F19 mapping and confirmed the extra actions occur on Boot Camp.
A maintainer stated that the current low-level hook cannot reliably suppress lower-level driver behavior while preserving the remapped keystroke.
The reporter confirmed the issue persisted in October 2024.
inferences: A driver-level filter could potentially intercept the physical F-key before Boot Camp, but this is outside the currently available Keyboard Manager architecture.
issue_context.analysis: The report is reproducible only with niche Apple Boot Camp hardware and the platform driver is the source of the additional action. Preserve the limitation accurately without claiming that the user should change Boot Camp settings or that a PowerToys fix shipped.
initial_investigation: Read the original report and six comments, including the reporter's clarification, maintainer architectural response, and reporter confirmation that the behavior persisted.
No linked fix or available driver-level implementation was found.
